scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion was 88% (vs 95% target) covering 9,200 manual-read accounts for period 2026-08..09.

F-02.statement: 1,785 disputed bills are associated with ACTUAL meter reads, per billing-db.disputed_bills_by_read_type.

F-03.statement: 1,240 disputed bills are associated with ESTIMATED meter reads, per billing-db.disputed_bills_by_read_type.

F-04.statement: billing-db.tariff_change_log returned 0 records, indicating no logged tariff rate changes.

F-05.statement: Dispute tickets rose from 610 (Jun 2026) and 590 (Jul 2026) to 1180 (Aug 2026) and 1260 (Sep 2026), per crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly.

F-06.statement: CRM dispute response times across 2,440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-07.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes, executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is mainly a Customer Service response-capacity problem; auto-answering tickets with an AI agent would resolve it without needing to find a billing-pipeline defect.

H-RULE-CHANGE-ERROR.statement: A change to billing import validation rules (e.g., estimate-substitution logic) around August produced systematically wrong bills, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read delivery or validation failures at the vendor (ORG-AMI) caused missing or invalid reads, forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter read failures or incomplete routes by the contracted field service (ORG-FIELD) caused missing/incorrect reads, feeding estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-LEGITIMATE-BILL-CHANGE.statement: Bills issued since August are accurate but reflect a legitimate tariff or usage increase, so disputes reflect customer surprise rather than billing errors.

H-ACTUAL-READ-BILL-ERROR.statement: The majority of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025) are associated with ACTUAL, non-estimated reads, suggesting a billing calculation or tariff-application defect on actual-read bills distinct from read-collection/estimate-substitution failures.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual-read route completion was 88% against a 95% target for 9,200 manual-read accounts over Aug-Sep 2026, a measurable shortfall in completed manual meter reads during the dispute-surge period. This is consistent with incomplete routes forcing estimate substitution on a subset of manual-read accounts, but it does not by itself establish that those shortfalls produced the wrong bills driving the dispute surge.

billing-db shows 3,025 disputed bills split by read type: 1,785 (59%) involve ACTUAL reads and 1,240 (41%) involve ESTIMATED reads. So the majority of disputed bills are not tied to estimate substitution, which is the shared causal mechanism behind the AMI-failure, field-failure and rule-change hypotheses.

billing-db.tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate changes are logged in the system. This weakens the 'legitimate tariff change' limb of H-LEGITIMATE-BILL-CHANGE but says nothing about usage increases or tariff-application logic defects.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) claims no tariff change occurred this year; this is an unverified stakeholder statement, not authoritative evidence, but it echoes the same question already answered by E-03 (0 tariff changes logged in billing-config).

crm-tickets.dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 and 590 disputes in June and July 2026, then 1180 and 1260 in August and September 2026 — roughly a 2x jump coincident with August. This confirms the magnitude and timing of the dispute surge referenced in the initial request, but says nothing about its cause.

crm-tickets reports 2,440 dispute tickets with median response time 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA. This shows response handling is currently meeting its target despite the ticket-volume surge (E-05), undercutting the premise that slow response handling is driving or compounding the dispute problem.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims a staffing shortfall of three readers since July causes late routes and estimate substitution for affected customers; this is an unverified stakeholder claim, not evidence, and SH-FIELD has a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias toward attributing problems to staffing.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Service contract §4.2 (E-08) states the utility may request route priority changes but they are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update actions against field-dispatch. This document addresses governance of a protected action, not the causal diagnosis of the dispute surge.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes identifies 14 specific routes with distinct (per-route) completion rates, one sampled at 70% completion for route R-00, giving route-level granularity behind the aggregate 88% manual-read completion shortfall already recorded in E-01; it does not by itself quantify how much of the 41% ESTIMATED-read dispute share these lagging routes explain.

U-SURGE-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT.question: Does the 3,025 disputed-bills read-type breakdown (E-02) correspond specifically to the Aug-Sep surge window, or does it span a broader/different period, which determines whether the ACTUAL-read mechanism actually explains the doubling?
U-SURGE-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT.decision_impact: If the breakdown isn't surge-specific, the actual-read billing-defect premise may not explain the Aug-Sep doubling and competing mechanisms need re-weighing.
U-SURGE-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT.resolution_path: Re-query billing-db.disputed_bills_by_read_type filtered to the Aug-Sep 2026 window specifically.
U-SURGE-PERIOD-ALIGNMENT.safe_placeholder: Proceed treating actual-read billing calculation as the primary lead while keeping field/AMI read failures as secondary candidates pending this check.

U-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING.question: Did a billing import validation/calculation rule (DA-RULES) change in or shortly before August 2026 that would explain wrong actual-read bills?
U-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING.decision_impact: Confirms or disproves the specific calculation-defect mechanism and determines where and how a fix must be made.
U-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule change log for changes dated around July-August 2026.
U-RULE-CHANGE-TIMING.safe_placeholder: Treat the defect location as unconfirmed; do not propose any specific config/code fix or bill adjustment until this log is reviewed.

U-FIELD-ESTIMATE-CONTRIBUTION.question: To what extent does the route-completion shortfall (88% vs 95%, E-01) explain the 41% of disputed bills tied to ESTIMATED reads, versus field staffing shortage (CL-03/E-07, unverified stakeholder claim) as its root cause?
U-FIELD-ESTIMATE-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether a secondary fix track (field routing/staffing) is needed alongside the billing-calculation fix, and whether any field-dispatch change would trigger K-DISPATCH approval.
U-FIELD-ESTIMATE-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Correlate route-log completion shortfalls to the specific accounts generating ESTIMATED-read disputes.
U-FIELD-ESTIMATE-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Do not propose any field dispatch route changes until this correlation is confirmed; push_route_update stays out of scope.

U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Follow up with ORG-AMI vendor on export access provisioning; retry mdms-export once tool_health returns to HEALTHY.
U-AMI-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Exclude AMI-read verification from the current investigation path until vendor access is provisioned; rely on billing-side evidence (E-02) in the interim.

problem_definition.requested_solution: SH-CS (Customer Service Director) requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01, initial request).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05).
59% of disputed bills (1,785 of 3,025) are tied to ACTUAL, non-estimated meter reads rather than ESTIMATED reads (E-02).
Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target over Aug-Sep 2026 for 9,200 manual-read accounts (E-01).
CRM dispute response times remain within the 3.0-day SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d across 2,440 tickets) despite the ticket-volume surge (E-06).
problem_definition.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1,220/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05) primarily because the billing-import/calculation step is producing incorrect charges on bills tied to ACTUAL (non-estimated) meter reads: 59% of disputed bills (1,785/3,025) involve ACTUAL reads (E-02), which rules out estimate-substitution mechanisms (AMI read failure, field read failure, rule-change-on-estimates) as the dominant driver, while a logged tariff change (E-03) and slow response handling (E-06, within SLA) are also ruled out as causes.
